POC / technical notes:
- Workload: near-real-time support chat + doc search; peak QPS 80-120 for embeddings rerank requests, sustained QPS ~25.
- Latency targets: 95th < 350ms for short-turn chat responses; p50 generation time target < 150ms where possible. Throughput priority for batching on embeddings.
- Cost sensitivity: high — product team estimates current monthly ML spend pain point; target is to cut inference unit cost by 30-50% vs baseline.
- Model preferences: open Llama-derivative family and a smaller GPT-like variant for reranking. Want ability to route to cheaper variants during peak.
- Routing/fallback: need policy for hosted->dedicated fallback, region-aware routing, graceful model degrade.
- Security: SSO required, audit logs and KMS for encryption, retention controls and EU residency for EU customers.

POC findings from cost workshop:
- Batching: embedding batching reduced per-request GPU time by ~28% in test runs (batch size 64).
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for common prompts decreased token generation by ~12% on chat flows.
- Quantization: int8 profile tested on candidate model — reduced GPU memory footprint ~40%, cost estimate improvement ~30% with small latency increase (~+8%). Need accuracy regression tests across core prompt set.
- Unit economics: Maya presented three pricing buckets with expected per-1000-token costs. Customer wants a worked example for their weekly traffic patterns.

Quotes / Callouts:
- "If we can get predictable unit costs and a clear migration path from Hosted to Dedicated, we'll sign an annual commit." — Ben Keller (Head Product)
- Legal: "Need contractual clause for EU data residency and encryption at rest with customer KMS."
